language.title: Language
language.label: Language
language.hint: Match Windows uses the first of your Windows languages that {{brand}} has, or English. Dates and numbers follow your Windows region. Languages other than English were translated by machine; corrections are welcome.

progress.title: Progress
progress.hint: Home shows the tasks you finished this week, the last eight weeks and how many working days in a row you finished something. Your year prints a year of finished work. Nothing is scored.

workingHours.title: Working hours
workingHours.description: The Calendar's Week opens on these hours and shades the rest of the day.
workingHours.endAfterStart: The end must be after the start.

general.selectBoxPressKeys: Select the box and press the keys you want, such as Ctrl+Alt+N.
general.useStandardWindowsTitle: Use the standard Windows title bar
general.showsWindowsOwnTitle: Shows Windows' own title bar and menu bar instead of {{brand}}'s. Applies the next time {{brand}} starts.
general.closingWindowHidesNotification: Closing the window hides {{brand}} in the notification area. To quit, use its icon there or File › Exit.
general.startsNotificationAreaWithout: {{brand}} starts in the notification area, without opening its window.
general.opensWindowWhenSign: {{brand}} opens its window when you sign in to Windows.
general.keyOpensQuickAdd: A key that opens Quick add from any app, while {{brand}} is running.
general.systemFollowsWindowsLight: System follows Windows' light or dark mode.
general.compactMakesTextControls: Compact makes text and controls smaller so more fits on screen.
general.windowsAccentColourCan: Your Windows accent colour can't be made readable with white text, so {{brand}} blue is used.
general.windowsAccentColourDarkened: The Windows accent colour is darkened or lightened where needed so text on it stays readable.
general.archivedRemovedProjectOpens: An archived or removed project opens Home instead.
general.projectHadOpenLast: The project you had open last
general.useCtrlAltLetter: Use Ctrl or Alt with a letter, a number or a function key.
general.backgroundMode: Keep {{brand}} running in the background, for reminders
general.backgroundModeWithAgents: Keep {{brand}} running in the background, for reminders and agents
general.keyStartsSnip: A key that snips part of the screen and opens Quick add with the picture, while {{brand}} is running.
general.snipKeyHint: Select the box and press the keys you want, such as Ctrl+Alt+S.
general.notTheQuickAddKey: Quick add already uses this key. Choose a different one.

tips.title: Tips and tours
tips.hint: Small notes that point out what a part of the window does, once each, starting in the demo project. They never block anything, and each one can be closed.
tips.resetDoneBody: Tips you closed for good, and the tour's invitation, will show again.

backupsSection.backupsHoldProjectsPlans: Backups hold your projects' plans, Library, AI drafts and settings. Agent workspaces are not included. A backup's saved AI key only works for this Windows user on this PC.
backupsSection.willRestartCurrentData: {{brand}} will restart. Your current data is saved first.
backupsSection.secondPlaceHint: A copy of each backup on a USB drive, another disk, a network share or a synced folder, kept as the backups here are.
backupsSection.notCopiedYet: Not copied yet. The next backup is copied to {{folder}}.
backupsSection.copyFailed: The last copy failed: {{folder}} could not be reached. {{brand}} tries again at the next backup.
backupsSection.syncedBy: This folder is in {{service}}: the backups will be stored by {{service}} too.
backupsSection.stoppedCopying: Backups are no longer copied. Copies already there stay.
backupsSection.secondPlaceBackupsHint: Restoring one copies it into the backups folder here first, then restarts {{brand}} to restore it.
backupsSection.noSecondPlaceBackups: No backups there, or the folder cannot be reached.

aboutSection.looksNewVersionEach: {{brand}} looks for a new version each time it starts.
aboutSection.newVersionDownloadsBackground: A new version downloads in the background. {{brand}} never restarts without asking.
aboutSection.tryNewVersionsBefore: Try new versions before everyone else. They may have more problems.
aboutSection.builtOpenSourcePackages: {{brand}} is built with open source packages. Each is listed with its licence.
aboutSection.projectManagerKeepsData: A project manager that keeps your data on this computer unless you choose to share it: no account needed and no tracking. {{brand}} only reads your project folders. It changes one only when you accept an agent's changes or ask it to create a new project folder.
aboutSection.copiesVersionsCountsEnd: Copies versions, counts and the end of the log for a bug report. Your name, keys and tokens are removed, and project names are never included. Nothing is sent anywhere.
aboutSection.portableWhichDoesNot: This is the portable {{brand}}, which does not update itself. Download the new version when you want it.
aboutSection.updatesOffDevelopmentBuilds: Updates are off in development builds.
aboutSection.versionInstallsWhenAgents_one: Version {{version}} installs when the agents finish ({{count}} agent working).
aboutSection.versionInstallsWhenAgents_other: Version {{version}} installs when the agents finish ({{count}} agents working).
aboutSection.versionReadyAgentsWorking_one: Version {{version}} is ready. {{count}} agent working: restarting now stops them.
aboutSection.versionReadyAgentsWorking_other: Version {{version}} is ready. {{count}} agents working: restarting now stops them.
aboutSection.versionReadyRestartUpdate: Version {{version}} is ready. Restart to update.
aboutSection.agentsWorkingWillStop_one: {{count}} agent working will stop. Their work so far is kept on their branches.
aboutSection.agentsWorkingWillStop_other: {{count}} agents working will stop. Their work so far is kept on their branches.
aboutSection.licencesCouldNotRead: The licences could not be read: {{error}}

devicesSection.keepInStep: Keep your projects, personal data and settings the same on all your PCs, through OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox or another folder your PCs share.
devicesSection.removeBody: {{name}} stops getting changes to your projects, personal data and settings. It keeps what it already has.
devicesSection.wantsToJoin: {{name}} wants to join. Check it shows {{code}}, then Allow.
devicesSection.addAnother: To add another PC, install {{brand}} there, choose Set up from my other device, then allow it here.
devicesSection.setUpFromOther: Set up from my other device
devicesSection.waitingApproval: On your other PC, open Settings › Devices and allow {{name}}. It shows {{code}}.
devicesSection.waitingForOther: Waiting for your other PC to allow this one…
devicesSection.anotherFolderHint: Any folder your PCs share, such as one on a network drive.
devicesSection.driveHint: Kept in your Google Drive, with no folder on this PC.
devicesSection.r2Hint: Kept in your own Cloudflare R2 bucket, with no folder on this PC.
devicesSection.notFoundYet: Already set up on another PC? {{brand}} looks for it in OneDrive, Google Drive and Dropbox. If it's in another folder, or hasn't finished syncing to this PC, choose its folder.
devicesSection.noDeviceCanAllow: Don’t have your other device any more?
devicesSection.startNewExplain: If the device that made this space is gone, start a new space here instead. The old one in {{place}} moves into a folder named “Old personal space” with today's date; nothing is deleted. Any device still using the old space has to join the new one.
devicesSection.moveHint: Copy your space and projects into your R2 bucket, then every device syncs there. The copy in {{place}} stays as it is; nothing is deleted.
devicesSection.moved: Your space is now in your R2 bucket, and your other devices switch the next time they sync. The old copy is still where it was; delete it yourself once you are sure.
devicesSection.movedKept: Projects that stayed where they were: {{count}}
devicesSection.moveFailed: The move stopped: {{error}} Nothing was lost. Try again to carry on where it stopped.
devicesSection.movedElsewhere: Another device moved your space into an R2 bucket. Set up the same bucket under Advanced sync so this PC can follow.

connectionsSection.letsAssistantPlan: Lets an assistant you trust plan for you: it can read and change tasks, milestones and Library items through {{brand}}'s automation API, with a token you create for each project. It works whether AI agents are on or off.
connectionsSection.whileOff: While it is off, nothing listens and no assistant can connect.
connectionsSection.listensThisComputer: {{brand}} listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1), and answers only requests that carry a project's token.
connectionsSection.changingPort: Changing it restarts the automation API. Connected assistants need the new address.
connectionsSection.eachProjectToken: Each project has its own token, and a token reaches only its project.
connectionsSection.assistantCan: An AI assistant or coding tool that speaks the Model Context Protocol (MCP) can read this project's plan, add and change tasks and milestones, and file notes in the Library, with this token's rights. It cannot reach AI agents' work.
connectionsSection.assistantPrivacy: An assistant may send what it reads from {{brand}} to its own AI provider. Connect only an assistant you trust with this project.
connectionsSection.createTokenFirst: Create an automation token to connect an assistant.
connectionsSection.httpConfigHint: The token is hidden here; Copy puts the full text on the clipboard.
connectionsSection.stdioConfigHint: No token: {{brand}} reads it when the assistant starts the command. {{brand}} must be running.

advancedSection.contextSizeDescription: {{brand}} AI reads your project's files when it answers. It sends up to about 60% of the model's context as files and leaves the rest for your conversation.
advancedSection.contextSizeHint: How much your model can read at once. Check your provider's model page; 100,000 suits most.
advancedSection.projectsWhoseFolderGit: For projects whose folder is a Git repository, {{brand}} reads new commits. It never commits or changes your branches.
advancedSection.commitsReadTime: Commits to read at a time
advancedSection.noticesWhenFilesChange: {{brand}} notices when files change in a project's folder (the file watcher). It only reads; it never changes your files.
advancedSection.noProjectHasLinked: No project has a linked folder, so there is nothing to watch.
advancedSection.onePatternPerLine: One pattern per line, for example node_modules/** or *.log.
advancedSection.developerLogs: In development builds, every AI call {{brand}} makes, including the built-in agent's (opencode), is written in full to {{aiLog}} in the source folder. Released builds never write it. Errors always go to {{mainLog}} in {{brand}}'s data folder, and Settings › About › Copy diagnostics copies a redacted summary to share.
advancedSection.lastChange_comment: {{when}} is a relative time: “5 minutes ago”, “yesterday”.
advancedSection.versionHistoryDescription: Before {{brand}} changes your project folder, it saves your edits as a "Your edits" entry in History, so nothing is lost.
advancedSection.manageHistoryMyselfHint: {{brand}} stops saving "Your edits" entries, and asks before touching a file with unsaved edits instead.

dataSection.everythingStoresStaysComputer: Everything {{brand}} stores stays on this computer.
dataSection.dataFolderSynced: {{brand}}'s data folder is in {{service}}. {{service}} copying the database while {{brand}} has it open can damage it, so keep the data folder outside synced folders. Backups can still go to {{service}}: choose it as the second place under Backups.
dataSection.fileGitAgentActivity: File, Git and agent activity older than 30 days is deleted for good. Your tasks, Library and decisions are kept.
dataSection.agentCopiesAndHistoryDescription: Each task's agent works in its own copy of the project. Restore points and discarded work are kept for a while so you can undo or bring them back.
dataSection.keepRestorePointsFor: Keep restore points and discarded work for
dataSection.keepRestorePointsHint: After this they are removed. Entries in History stay.
dataSection.oldAgentFiles: Files from the old agent setup: {{size}}
dataSection.removeOldAgentFilesTitle: Remove the files from the old agent setup?
dataSection.removeOldAgentFilesBody: Their agent work has already moved to the new copies. Remove them once you are happy nothing is missing.
dataSection.couldntRemoveOldAgentFiles: Couldn't remove the old agent files

importGroup.bringTasksSpreadsheetCsv: Bring in tasks from a spreadsheet (CSV), a Trello board or an exported project. Export a project, or its tasks as CSV, from the project's More menu.
importGroup.eachImportListedHere: Each import is listed here, and can be undone in one step.

notificationsSection.remindersArriveWindowsNotification: Reminders arrive as a Windows notification and in your Inbox. They fire only while {{brand}} is running; any that come due while it is closed arrive together when it next starts.
notificationsSection.noWindowsNotificationsBetween: No Windows notifications between these times. Inbox items still arrive.
notificationsSection.weeklyReviewHint: On this day, a notification and an Inbox item say it is time for your weekly review. Finishing a review that week clears it.
notificationsSection.keepRemindingHint: For a reminder you set to keep reminding me: how long until its notification comes back, unless you choose otherwise when you add it.
notificationsSection.notificationsAppearCornerScreen: Shown by Windows, in the corner of your screen and in the Windows notification centre (Windows key + N), even while {{brand}} is minimised or in the background. They are separate from in-app notifications.
notificationsSection.projectsLinkedFolder: For projects with a linked folder.
notificationsSection.whenManyFilesChange: When many files change at once
notificationsSection.whenAgentStartsFinishes: When an agent starts or finishes
notificationsSection.whenAgentAsksQuestion: When an agent asks a question
notificationsSection.whenAgentsWorkWaiting: When an agent's work is waiting for review
notificationsSection.dayBeforeDueDate: The day before and on the due date
notificationsSection.focusDescription: A countdown on a task's timer. While it runs, desktop notifications wait, as in quiet hours; Inbox items still arrive.
notificationsSection.focusLengthHint: From 5 to 180 minutes. You can pick another length each time.
notificationsSection.focusChime: Chime when a focus or a break ends
notificationsSection.focusChimeHint: A soft chime made by {{brand}}; it follows Windows' volume and mute.
notificationsSection.inAppDescription: The messages that pop up in the bottom-right corner of {{brand}}'s window, such as "Moved to the recycle bin" with Undo. Up to three show at once. Every one is kept under the bell at the right of the status bar until {{brand}} closes, so you can read it or undo it later.
notificationsSection.inAppDurationHint: Pointing at one, or tabbing to it, keeps it there.
notificationsSection.inAppUndoHint: Off: a change you can take back, such as "Moved to the recycle bin", no longer pops up. It is still kept under the bell, with its Undo.
notificationsSection.whenMentioned: When someone mentions me in a comment
notificationsSection.whenFollowedTaskChanged: When someone else changes a task I follow
notificationsSection.whenSignOff: When someone asks me to sign something off, or answers my request

calendars.title: Calendars
calendars.description: Calendar files exported from Outlook, Google Calendar or Apple Calendar, or a calendar's private link. Their events show beside your tasks in the Calendar and on Home, read-only. {{brand}} reads a file only when you add or reload it.
calendars.none: No calendars yet. Export your calendar as an .ics file, then add it here to see your meetings beside your tasks.
calendars.name: Name
calendars.previewNone: This file has no events {{brand}} can show.
calendars.shownOnceHint: Some repeating events use a rule {{brand}} does not follow, so they show only on their first day.
calendars.privacy: {{brand}} keeps this file where it is and reads it again only when you choose Reload. Its events are never searched or exported.
calendars.linkHint: Copy your calendar's private address: in Outlook it is under Shared calendars › Publish a calendar (the ICS link), in Google Calendar under the calendar's settings › Secret address in iCal format, and in Apple's iCloud Calendar under Share Calendar › Public Calendar. Anyone with the address can read the calendar, so keep it to yourself.
calendars.linkPrivacy: {{brand}} fetches only this address: now, a minute after it starts, every hour while it runs, and when you choose Refresh. It sends nothing else. The link is stored encrypted and never shown again in full.
calendars.accountTitle: Add a calendar from an account
calendars.accountDescription: Its events show read-only beside your tasks and update on the same schedule as calendar links.
calendars.accountPrivacy: {{brand}} reads events from 60 days ago to a year ahead, straight from the provider, and keeps them on this computer only.

daysOff.title: Days off
daysOff.description: Days nobody works, such as bank holidays, and days one person is away. Reschedule, Workload, the Calendar, the Timeline and date fields skip or show them. Weekends follow each person's working days.
daysOff.noneForEveryone: No days off for everyone yet. Add bank holidays here, or import a holiday calendar file.
daysOff.name: Name
daysOff.lastDayHint: Leave empty for a single day
daysOff.lastBeforeFirst: The last day can't be before the first
daysOff.previewCount_one: {{count}} all-day event becomes a day off.
daysOff.previewNone: This file has no all-day events to add.
daysOff.previewReplaces_one: It replaces {{count}} day off from an earlier load of this file.
daysOff.previewReplaces_other: It replaces {{count}} days off from an earlier load of this file.
daysOff.skippedTimed: has a time, not a whole day
daysOff.skippedRepeat: repeats in a way that can't be read

teams.title: Teams
teams.description: Name groups of people from your address book, such as a design team or a site crew, and pick who leads each. Teams are yours alone: they give nobody any access, are not shared with the people in a project, and follow you to your own other computers. Use them to filter Workload.
teams.none: No teams yet. Make one to group the people you work with.
teams.deleteBody: The team is removed. The people in it stay in your address book.
teams.name: Name
teams.noPeople: Add people to your address book first.

peopleSection.peopleAssignTasksThey: The people you assign tasks to. They are names in {{brand}}, not accounts, and every project shares them.
peopleSection.chooseSomeoneElseFirst: Choose someone else as you first
peopleSection.name: Name
peopleSection.leaveEmptyUseNames: Leave empty to use the name's.
peopleSection.weeklyCapacityHint: Hours a week this person plans to work, for Workload. Leave empty for none.
peopleSection.chooseWorkingDay: Choose at least one working day.

projectsSection.archivedProjectsHiddenSidebar: Archived projects are hidden from the sidebar and Home until you bring them back.
projectsSection.projectHoldsTasksMilestones: A project holds your tasks, milestones, documents and decisions. Create one to begin.

taskTemplatesGroup.title: Task templates
taskTemplatesGroup.description: Single tasks saved to make again, with their subtasks: for one project or every project.
taskTemplatesGroup.noneHint: Open a task and choose Save as task template… from its menu.
taskTemplatesGroup.playbooksDescription: Task templates for agents: Run playbook makes the task and queues it, with the playbook's model, plan first choice and extra instructions.
taskTemplatesGroup.isPlaybookHint: A task template for agents, listed under Playbooks and offered in Run playbook.

templatesGroup.templatesSavedProjectSave: Templates you saved from a project. Save one from a project's More menu; start a project from one in New project.
templatesGroup.openProjectsMoreMenu: Open a project's More menu and choose Save as template… to reuse its plan.

githubToken.title: GitHub
githubToken.description: Tasks can link GitHub issues and pull requests, and Import tasks can bring in a repository's issues. Public repositories work without a token, within GitHub's limit of 60 requests an hour. A token lets {{brand}} read private repositories and raises the limit.
githubToken.whatIsSent: {{brand}} only reads from GitHub, and only when you open a task with links, press Refresh, link an issue or import. It sends the repository and issue number, and your token when one is saved. Nothing is ever written to GitHub.
githubToken.tokenHint: A fine-grained personal access token with read-only access to Issues and Pull requests (and Metadata) on the repositories you link. It is encrypted on this computer when Windows can, and never shown again.
githubToken.removeBody: Private repositories stop working until you add a token again. Links you already made stay.

boardDefaults.title: Board for all projects
boardDefaults.description: What a project's board opens with until the project keeps a default of its own, and the views offered in every project. Change them in Customise board on any board.

policy.aiOff: Your organisation has turned {{brand}} AI off on this PC.
policy.agentsOff: Your organisation has turned AI agents off on this PC.

syncServer.title: Sync server
syncServer.description: Share projects through a server in place of a synced folder. Everything {{brand}} keeps there is encrypted, so the server can't read it.
syncServer.usingKey: Shares through {{server}} with an access key.
syncServer.forgetBody: Projects shared through it stop syncing on this PC until you set it up again. Nothing is deleted from the server.
syncServer.addressHint: The server's owner gives you this.
syncServer.keyHint: Paste the key the server's owner gave you. It's kept protected on this PC and never shown again.
syncServer.keySaved: A key is saved. Paste a new one to replace it, or leave this empty to keep it.
syncServer.scopeHint: The server's API scope, such as api://ostler-sync/sync.
syncServer.connectAccountFirst: Connect a Microsoft work account in Accounts above first.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Connect the accounts your calendars, contacts and files are in. Nothing is sent to any of them until you connect one, and you can remove one at any time.

signInHint.google: Your browser opens to sign in to Google. {{brand}} asks to read: {{gives}}.
signInHint.microsoft: Your browser opens to sign in to Microsoft. {{brand}} asks to read: {{gives}}.
signInHint.dropbox: Your browser opens to sign in to Dropbox. {{brand}} asks to read: {{gives}}.

accounts.finishInBrowser: Finish signing in in your browser, then come back here.
accounts.registrationPolicy: Signing in uses your organisation's app registration.
accounts.needsRegistration: {{brand}} isn't registered with this provider yet. If your organisation has its own app registration for {{brand}}, enter its client ID to sign in with it.

clientIdHint.google: From Google Cloud › APIs & Services › Credentials, a Desktop app client.
clientIdHint.microsoft: The Application (client) ID of a Microsoft Entra app that allows public client flows, with http://localhost as a redirect address.
clientIdHint.dropbox: The App key of a Dropbox app that uses PKCE.

accounts.clientSecretHint: Google gives Desktop app clients one. It is stored encrypted.
accounts.icloudHint: Apple has no sign-in for other apps. Make an app-specific password at account.apple.com › Sign-In and Security, and enter it here with your Apple ID. {{brand}} reads your iCloud calendars and contacts with it.
accounts.caldavHint: For Fastmail, Nextcloud, Synology and other CalDAV and CardDAV servers. Your provider's help pages give the address.
accounts.appPasswordHint: Many providers ask for an app password rather than your normal one. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
accounts.appPasswordHintIcloud: An app-specific password, not your Apple ID password. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
accounts.removeBody: {{brand}} stops reading from this account and forgets how to sign in to it. Calendars and contacts it brought in stop updating.
accounts.browserDone: You're signed in. You can close this tab and go back to {{brand}}.
accounts.browserFailed: Signing in didn't finish. Close this tab and try again in {{brand}}.

webhooks.title: Tell the team
webhooks.description: Post this project's news to a channel: a status update, a milestone done, a review waiting. Only the project's name and the news itself are sent.

kind.generic: Another service (Zapier, Make, n8n, Power Automate)

help.teams: In the Teams channel, choose Workflows › “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”, finish it, and copy the address it gives.
help.slack: In Slack, make an app with Incoming Webhooks for the channel and copy its webhook address.
help.discord: In the Discord channel's settings, choose Integrations › Webhooks › New Webhook › Copy Webhook URL.
help.generic: {{brand}} posts JSON with the event, the project, a title, the text and the time.

webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.urlHint: Anyone with the address can post to the channel. {{brand}} stores it encrypted and never shows it again in full.
webhooks.testText: This channel will get this project's news.
webhooks.removeBody: Nothing more is posted there. The channel itself is not changed.

calendarWrite.title: Time blocks in your calendar
calendarWrite.description: Copy your time blocks as busy events into a calendar, so others see the time is taken.
calendarWrite.stopBody: The events {{brand}} wrote for your time blocks are deleted from that calendar. Your blocks stay here.
calendarWrite.chooseTitle: Copy time blocks into a calendar
calendarWrite.chooseDescription: Blocks from a week ago to 90 days ahead are copied as busy events. Moving or removing a block here changes its event there.
calendarWrite.privacy: Each event holds the task's title and the project's name, nothing else. Change an event there and {{brand}} puts it back as the block says.

taskList.title: My tasks in To Do or Google Tasks
taskList.description: Copy the open tasks assigned to you into a Microsoft To Do or Google Tasks list. Tick one off there and it is marked done here.
taskList.stopBody: The open items {{brand}} made in that list are deleted. Your tasks stay here.
taskList.chooseTitle: Copy my tasks into a list
taskList.chooseDescription: Your open tasks in enabled projects are copied with their title, project and due date. {{brand}}'s version wins, except that ticking an item off marks its task done.
taskList.privacy: Each item holds the task's title, its project's name and its due date, nothing else.

deletePersonDialog.title: Delete {{personName}}?
deletePersonDialog.sharedMember: {{personName}} is a member of a shared project. Remove them in that project's Sharing settings first.
deletePersonDialog.rulesTurnedOff: Rules that name them are turned off.
deletePersonDialog.cantBeUndone: This can't be undone. Comments, activity and time they logged stay, without their name.

email.title: Email
email.description: Your own email server (SMTP), such as your email provider's, so {{brand}} can email an invite for you. Nothing is sent until you choose to.
email.serverHint: Such as smtp.office365.com or smtp.gmail.com. Your email provider's help says which.
email.usernameHint: Usually your email address. Leave it empty for a server that needs no sign-in.
email.passwordHint: Many providers want an app password here, made in your account's security settings. It is encrypted on this PC and never shown again.
email.passwordKept: A password is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
email.fromNameHint: How you appear in their inbox. Optional.
email.removeBody: {{brand}} forgets the server and its password. Invites can still be copied and sent yourself.
email.testBody: This test came from {{brand}} through {{server}}. Invites you email from a project's Sharing go the same way.

advancedSync.title: Advanced sync: Cloudflare R2
advancedSync.description: Copy your personal space to your own Cloudflare R2 bucket, so your phone can sync through it instead of Google Drive. Everything in it stays sealed with your projects' keys, so Cloudflare can't read it, and a new device still has to be allowed here with its code.
advancedSync.needsSpace: Set up Keep my devices in step above first, in a folder on this PC. That folder is what gets copied.
advancedSync.how: In the Cloudflare dashboard: R2 › Create bucket, then R2 › Manage API tokens › Create token with Object Read & Write for that bucket only. Paste the account ID, the token's access key ID and secret here.
advancedSync.endpointHint: Leave empty for R2. For R2's EU jurisdiction or another S3-compatible store, its https address.
advancedSync.secretSaved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
advancedSync.checkEvery: Look for changes from your other devices
advancedSync.onlySyncNow: Only when I press Sync now
advancedSync.uploadSoon: Send this PC's changes soon after they happen (within a minute)
advancedSync.uploadSoonHint: Off: they go up at the next look or Sync now.
advancedSync.costNote: Looking costs one small request; the bucket is only listed when another device changed something. A person's use stays well inside R2's free tier.
advancedSync.testOk: The bucket answered. Ostler can read and write it.
advancedSync.skipped_one: {{count}} shared project is kept outside this folder, so it isn't copied.
advancedSync.skipped_other: {{count}} shared projects are kept outside this folder, so they aren't copied.
advancedSync.exportHint: For your phone (Settings › Advanced sync) or another PC. Send the code and the passphrase separately.
advancedSync.removeBody: This PC stops copying and forgets the bucket's keys. Nothing is deleted from the bucket or from this PC.
